page: Amazon Web Services t3.small is a burstable performance instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, yielding 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 2.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing 1.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU includes a 33 MB L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, AES cryptography, and FMA. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the t3.small in the lower performance tier, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU metrics falling into the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests show 70.12 GB/sec for cached small blocks, which drops to 8.1 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect entry-level capabilities, with a Passmark CPU score of 1893.8 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 15.04 GB/sec. Redis SET operations achieve 1.64 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 1.22 GB/sec.

Given its burstable CPU allocation and entry-level hardware profile, the t3.small offers a highly cost-efficient option for workloads with low baseline CPU utilization that require occasional bursts of higher performance. The primary tradeoff is the shared-core architecture and limited memory capacity, which makes it unsuitable for sustained heavy compute or memory-intensive applications. This instance is best suited for low-traffic web servers, small microservices, development and testing environments, or basic background scripting tasks.
